title: Frontend app shell/navigation — non-blocking review follow-ups
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #62 (frontend-app-shell-navigation), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so they aren't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: AppShell.tsx wraps a `<Box component="nav">` around NavDrawer, whose own root is `<List component="nav" aria-label="main navigation">` — this nests two `<nav>` landmarks inside each other on every render (desktop and mobile), which is discouraged by ARIA authoring practices and reads as duplicate/confusing navigation to a screen-reader user jumping by landmark. Drop `component="nav"` from one of the two (the outer Box is only a layout wrapper for width/flex sizing; the semantic `<nav>` belongs on NavDrawer's List).

AppShell.test.tsx re-declares its own `mockMatchMedia` MediaQueryList mock object almost field-for-field identical to the default mock already installed in tests/setup.ts. Extract a shared helper (e.g. exported from tests/setup.ts or a small test-utils module) so future tests needing the narrow-width override don't have to keep two copies in sync.

Reconsider AppErrorBoundary's placement under components/layout/ vs components/common/. It satisfies Frontend.md §3's common/ criterion (doesn't reference a position/ticker/signal — fully domain-agnostic), and an error-boundary wrapper is a generically reusable pattern in its own right (could later wrap an individual feature subtree, not just the whole app) even though it's only instantiated once today — the task's own decisions entry leaned on 'used once, same pattern as AppShell' as the rationale for layout/, which is exactly the instantiation-count reasoning that doesn't establish non-reusability. Revisit once frontend-common-components lands and common/'s Storybook conventions (including a story that deliberately throws to exercise the fallback) are established, to decide with those conventions in hand rather than pre-empting them.

decisions.decision: Fixed the nested `<nav>` landmark by removing `component="nav"` from AppShell.tsx's outer Box (now a plain layout Box/div), keeping the semantic `<nav>` role solely on NavDrawer's own `<List component="nav" aria-label="main navigation">`.
decisions.rationale: The outer Box exists purely for width/flex layout sizing around the responsive Drawer (permanent vs. temporary variant) and never itself needs to be discoverable as a landmark; NavDrawer's List is the actual semantic navigation content and already carries an aria-label. Removing the role from the Drawer-wrapper (rather than from NavDrawer's List) keeps the more descriptive, already-labeled landmark. Added a regression test (`AppShell.test.tsx`: 'exposes exactly one nav landmark, not a nested pair', asserting `getAllByRole('navigation')` has length 1) so this can't silently regress.

decisions.decision: Extracted the matchMedia mock into a new frontend/tests/mockMatchMedia.ts with two exports: `installDefaultMatchMedia(matches)` (a one-time property assignment, used by tests/setup.ts to provide jsdom's missing `window.matchMedia` globally) and `mockMatchMedia(matches)` (a `vi.spyOn`-based per-test override, used by AppShell.test.tsx to force the narrow/wide branch). Both share one private `createMatchMediaMock(query, matches)` object factory.
decisions.rationale: The two call sites have genuinely different needs, not just duplicated literals: the global default must work before any `matchMedia` property exists on `window` (jsdom doesn't implement it), which rules out `vi.spyOn` there since spyOn requires an existing method to wrap — hence a plain conditional assignment. A per-test override, by contrast, needs `vi.spyOn` so it composes with the existing `afterEach(() => vi.restoreAllMocks())` in AppShell.test.tsx and cleanly reverts between tests. Splitting into two thin functions over one shared object-factory keeps both call sites correct without hand-rolling the `MediaQueryList` shape (matches/media/onchange/add-remove-listener variants/dispatchEvent) more than once, which was the actual duplication the review flagged. Rejected alternative: a single function that always uses `vi.spyOn` — rejected because it can't run before jsdom exposes the property in the first place, which setup.ts needs.

decisions.decision: Moved AppErrorBoundary from components/layout/ to components/common/AppErrorBoundary/ (colocated .tsx + .test.tsx, unchanged, plus a new .stories.tsx with a 'renders children' story and a 'deliberately throws to exercise the fallback' story), and updated main.tsx's import accordingly.
decisions.rationale: Re-examined the two original candidate placements now that frontend-common-components has landed and established common/'s actual conventions (colocated test+story per component, one folder per component, no barrel yet). AppErrorBoundary passes Frontend.md §3's common/ test cleanly: it is fully domain-agnostic (no position/ticker/signal knowledge) and its behavior — catch a render-time throw in its subtree, show a fallback, offer a reset — is a generic pattern that could just as validly wrap a single feature subtree in the future as it currently wraps the whole app; single-instantiation-today was the prior task's stated rationale for layout/, and pr-reviewer's own review of PR #62 already flagged that reasoning as conflating current call-site count with actual reusability, which this task exists to resolve. The remaining candidate reason to keep it in layout/ (Frontend.md §3 lists AppShell.tsx/NavDrawer.tsx there) doesn't extend to AppErrorBoundary: that list isn't stated as closed, but more importantly layout/'s own definition in Frontend.md §3 is 'app shell, not reusable outside this app' — AppErrorBoundary is exactly not that, since nothing about it is app-shell- or routing-specific the way AppShell/NavDrawer's chrome and nav-item list are. Writing the 'deliberately throws' story turned out to be straightforward (a component whose render body just throws, passed as `children`), which was the concrete precedent this task was waiting on frontend-common-components to establish. Rejected alternative: leave it in layout/ on the grounds that it's still only instantiated once today — rejected for the reason above (that's an instantiation-count argument, not a reusability one, and is the exact reasoning PR #62's review called out as weak).

comments.summary: Minor/non-blocking: AppErrorBoundary's fallback UI hardcodes `minHeight: '100vh'` and 'reload the app' copy, a whole-app-page assumption baked into an otherwise domain-agnostic, generically-reusable component. This slightly undercuts the PR's own stated rationale for the common/ move ('could later wrap just a feature subtree') — a subtree-scoped instance would inherit full-viewport-sized fallback chrome. Tracked as a follow-up (frontend-app-shell-navigation-followups-followups) rather than blocking, since it doesn't affect current behavior (the component is only instantiated once, wrapping the whole app, where 100vh is correct today).

review.notes: Full review of PR #83, all three checklist items verified against the diff (git diff main...HEAD): (1) nested <nav> fix — AppShell.tsx's outer Box no longer carries component="nav", NavDrawer's List remains the sole landmark, with a new regression test asserting getAllByRole('navigation') has length 1; confirmed live in a real browser (Playwright/chromium against `npm run dev`) at both desktop width (1 landmark) and narrow width in both drawer-closed (0, temporary Drawer unmounted) and drawer-open (1, not nested) states — matches the fix exactly. (2) matchMedia dedup — frontend/tests/mockMatchMedia.ts now holds the single MediaQueryList mock shape behind installDefaultMatchMedia (setup.ts's global default) and mockMatchMedia (AppShell.test.tsx's per-test override); both call sites use it, no drift. (3) AppErrorBoundary moved to components/common/AppErrorBoundary/ with a colocated Storybook story (RendersChildren + CaughtError, the latter deliberately throwing to exercise the fallback) — verified both stories render correctly in a live Storybook instance (chromium screenshots), no console/page errors. Placement re-assessed per step 7a independent of the task's own decisions entry: AppErrorBoundary is fully domain-agnostic (no position/ticker/signal knowledge) and Frontend.md §3 defines layout/ as 'app shell, not reusable outside this app', which AppErrorBoundary's catch-any-render-crash behavior clearly isn't scoped to — common/ is the correct placement, not a genuinely arguable case. Backend: 488 tests passed, 99.84% coverage (pytest --cov=app --cov-fail-under=90; no backend files touched by this PR). Frontend: 193 tests passed across 35 files, 99.7%/99.6%/100%/99.7% stmt/branch/func/line coverage (vitest run --coverage), `npm run lint` clean, `npm run build` (tsc -b && vite build) clean. code-review skill (medium effort) found zero issues. No API route/schema touched, so no OpenAPI snapshot regeneration required. Browser walkthrough performed (this PR touches layout/nav components): golden path (desktop dashboard load, nav-link click to /portfolio, exactly one nav landmark throughout) and edge case (375px-wide viewport hamburger toggle open/close, drawer variant switch) both via a headless Chromium driven by a standalone Playwright script (no MCP browser tools were available in this session) against `npm run dev` + a locally running backend (`uvicorn app.main:app`); console/network monitored throughout — the only error surfaced was a pre-existing CORS rejection between the dev servers on different ports (`localhost:5173` -> `localhost:8000`, no CORS middleware configured in app/main.py), unrelated to this PR's diff and out of scope (not filed as a follow-up under this task since it isn't a finding about the reviewed change). One non-blocking finding (100vh fallback sizing, above) filed as a follow-up task per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule rather than left only as a PR comment. Decisions entries are well-formed (state what was decided and why, including explicitly rejected alternatives) for all three checklist items — no undecided 'decide X' checklist phrasing to cross-check. No pr_decision field existed on this task prior to this review, so nothing needed clearing.

pr_decision.notes: Re-ran backend (488 passed, 99.84% coverage, no backend files in diff) and frontend (193 passed/35 files, 99.7/99.6/100/99.7% stmt/branch/func/line, lint clean, build clean) suites myself — both match review.notes exactly. Read git diff origin/main...HEAD for every changed file: confirmed AppShell.tsx's outer Box dropped component="nav" (NavDrawer's List remains the sole landmark) with the new getAllByRole('navigation').toHaveLength(1) regression test; confirmed AppErrorBoundary now exists only under components/common/AppErrorBoundary/ (test file shows as a pure git rename, no stray copy left in components/layout/, no remaining import of the old path, main.tsx updated, new stories.tsx covers both a normal render and a deliberately-throwing case); confirmed the matchMedia dedup (single createMatchMediaMock factory backing both installDefaultMatchMedia and mockMatchMedia, no drift). The one non-blocking finding (AppErrorBoundary's 100vh fallback sizing) is correctly tracked as docs/tasks/frontend-app-shell-navigation-followups-followups.json, planned, depends_on this task, mirrored in index.json. Accept holds.
